plainName: Setting off a loss against income under another head
summary: A loss under one head that is left after setting it against the same head reduces income under the other heads in the same year. A loss from house property does so only up to a limit; the rest is carried forward.

routes.name: A loss against the other heads
routes.description: The other heads absorb the loss in a stated order, which the law does not fix.

routes.name: A house-property loss, up to the limit
routes.description: Only part of a house-property loss may be set against other heads in a year.

disqualifiers.description: In the default regime a house-property loss is not set off against another head, and the loss is treated as fully used.
A business loss is never set against salary.

enforcedBy.reason: the business head is deferred in the coverage register

disqualifiers.description: A loss on capital assets is never set against another head.

enforcedBy.reason: the capital-gains head is planned for a later item

disqualifiers.description: No loss is set against undisclosed income found in a search.

enforcedBy.reason: search cases are deferred in the coverage register
